evals.prompt: We're doing a retro on the checkout outage and I want something more engaging than reading the postmortem out loud. Take incident-postmortem.md and make it an interactive space-mission adventure page the team can click through, with the real facts (timeline, root cause, action items) still available behind the story. Output: outage-mission.html
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained HTML file in a space theme that retells the incident as a mission, stage by stage in timeline order, with pop-outs or reveals that surface the exact facts: the NaN timeout root cause, the 47 minute duration, the six action items with owners, and the lessons.
expectations: A single .html output file exists in the outputs directory
Works offline: no external scripts, stylesheets, fonts or images are loaded
Contains substantial inline SVG illustration (several scenes, dozens of shapes), not just icons
Has click-to-reveal pop-outs (dialog/modal/details/tooltip) that hide explanatory text until activated
Page renders in headless Chrome with real content (JS ran, >300 words of rendered text)
Has at least 5 distinct navigable stages/chapters (not one long scroll)
Pop-out text names the real thing behind the allegory (e.g. 'VPN', 'PostgreSQL', a command) in plain language, not more story
The narrative reads as a themed story in second person with a consistent allegory, not a summary with costume words
The stages follow the source document's order so a reader could act on it afterwards
States the real root cause: Number() on '8000ms' giving NaN for PAYMENT_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_MS
Gives the real impact figures: 47 minutes, ~6,400 customers, 1,100 abandoned quotes
Lists all six action items with their substance (readIntEnv, audit env vars, startup validation, health endpoint, latency canary, runbook)
Presents the timeline in order (provider slowdown 09:12 appears before rollback 09:47) and names the rollback version v2.30.4

evals.prompt: my junior devs find our git guide boring. can you turn git-basics.md into a pirate-themed interactive adventure book in html? one file i can drop in slack, with nice visuals, and the actual git commands should still be findable when you click on stuff. call it git-voyage.html
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained pirate-themed HTML adventure that covers the guide's sections (mental model, starting work, saving, sharing, staying current, undoing, things not to do) and makes every git command from the guide reachable verbatim through pop-outs or reveals.
expectations: A single .html output file exists in the outputs directory
Works offline: no external scripts, stylesheets, fonts or images are loaded
Contains substantial inline SVG illustration (several scenes, dozens of shapes), not just icons
Has click-to-reveal pop-outs (dialog/modal/details/tooltip) that hide explanatory text until activated
Page renders in headless Chrome with real content (JS ran, >300 words of rendered text)
Has at least 5 distinct navigable stages/chapters (not one long scroll)
Pop-out text names the real thing behind the allegory (e.g. 'VPN', 'PostgreSQL', a command) in plain language, not more story
The narrative reads as a themed story in second person with a consistent allegory, not a summary with costume words
The stages follow the source document's order so a reader could act on it afterwards
Every core command from the guide is present verbatim (switch -c, add -p, rebase origin/main, --force-with-lease, reflog, restore --staged, gh pr create --draft, rebase --abort)
Covers the guide's sections: mental model (staging area), branching, committing (Conventional Commits), sharing (draft PR), rebasing, undoing, things not to do (secrets)
Preserves the safety rules: never plain --force on shared branches, do not commit secrets, do not commit to main
